meta.title: اختبار الفصل الأول في اللغة الإنجليزية (النموذج 3)
topics: reading: Make peace — peer mediation at school

paper:
Read the text carefully then do the activities.

In many schools around the world, students are trained to become "peer mediators". When two classmates have a conflict, a mediator meets them in a quiet room. The mediator does not judge or punish anyone. Instead, he listens to both sides and helps them find a solution together.

The results are often impressive. In some schools, fights in the playground have dropped by half. Teachers say that students learn to express their feelings with words instead of violence. "If everybody learnt to listen, there would be fewer conflicts," explains Amina, a sixteen-year-old mediator.

Of course, mediation cannot solve every problem. Serious cases still need the help of adults. But it gives young people a powerful message: peace is not only the absence of war; it is something we build every day.

Part One — A. Comprehension (7 pts)

  1. Choose the right title: a) Fights in schools b) Students who make peace c) Punishing bad students
  2. True or false? a) The mediator punishes the student who is wrong. b) Fights decreased in some schools. c) Mediation can solve all problems.
  3. What do the underlined words refer to? «he listens» (§1) ; «them» (§1)

Part One — B. Text exploration (7 pts)

  1. Find in the text opposites of: a) noisy (§1) b) increased (§2)
  2. Add a prefix to form opposites: a) fair b) agree c) possible
  3. Complete with the right form of the verbs: If I (be) a mediator, I (help) my classmates.
  4. Classify the words according to the stressed syllable: conflict (n.) – solution – impressive

Part Two — Written expression (6 pts)

Two of your friends had a quarrel and no longer speak to each other. Write a short paragraph (8–10 lines) explaining what you would do to help them make peace. Use the conditional type 2.
